subject: new case study: Jacobians and the MLE vs. Bayes

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: new case study: Jacobians and the MLE vs. Bayes
parts:
I finally got around to writing up the effects of Jacobians
on MLEs (breaks them) vs. Bayesian posteriors (preserves them),
which is why we say that Bayes is invariant to reparameterization
with appropriate Jacobian adjustments, but MLEs aren't.

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies/mle-params.html

The case study also talks about how not including the Jacobian
preserves the MLE, so they're invariant in another sense, leading
to potential terminological confusion.

Also, if anyone else wants to contribute case studies, we're ready
to receive them.

- Bob

P.S. Here's the abstract from the case studies page:

Maximum Likelihood, Bayesian Posteriors, and Reparameterization
---------------------------------------------------------------

When changing variables, a Jacobian adjustment needs to be provided to preserve the probability distributions of quantities of interest, incuding Bayesian posteriors. With appropriate Jacobians, Bayesian inference is invariant to the parameterization. In contrast, applying the appropriate Jacobian adjustment leads to different maximum likelihood estimates, whereas skipping the Jacobians leaves them unchanged. In this note, we contrast three simple repeated binary trial models, varying only by parameterization: (a) direct probability parameterization, (b) log odds parameterization without Jacobian adjustment, (c) log odds parameterization with Jacobian adjustment. Models (a) and (b) provide the same MLE, whereas model (c) has a different MLE. In contrast, models (a) and (c) provide the same Bayesian posterior, whereas model (b) differs.

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies/mle-params.html

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] new case study: Jacobians and the MLE vs. Bayes
parts:
OK, that was a bit fast off the cuff. I went back and revised it,
so it should read more smoothly. And it provides an example plot
of the change of variables in question with an R simulation. The
link's the same:

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies/mle-params.html

Comments are more than welcome. It's a tricky subject given
the interplay of MLE, posterior modes, and expectations/quantiles
with and without Jacobians.

- Bob

parts:
The most recent draft looks good, in particular because it is careful
to compare proper expectations to posterior modes. But I would
change the name of the case study to avoid referencing MLE
altogether which induces much pedantry and confusion.
